notes:
High-level: CodeLattice builds an in-IDE copilot and a hosted code search product used by engineering teams at scale. Primary ask: 1) ultra-low latency streaming completions for in-editor suggestions (tail latency target < 50ms for single-line completions), 2) reliable background pipelines to refresh repo embeddings (monorepo = ~500k files, nightly + incremental throughout day), 3) version pinning for reproducible assistant behavior across releases, and 4) SSO + strict audit logs for enterprise customers.

Timeline / recent activity:
- 2026-01-20: Intro call (AE Evelyn) - product overview, high-level infra needs.
- 2026-02-02: Technical deep-dive with SE (Ravi) - discussed batching, KV cache for completion, model variants for fallback.
- 2026-02-18: POC kickoff meeting (ff_2026-02-18_3b9f42). SE asked for dataset sample (2M tokens) and representative trace for completion QPS.
- 2026-03-05: Security sync (ff_2026-03-05_a8c117) - requested SOC2 evidence, KMS integration pattern, and retention controls. Submitted PIA doc to security (drive:/security/CL-privacy-impact-assessment-v2).
- 2026-03-10: Submitted initial perf results from hosted API microbench; customer requested Dedicated run to validate tail latency under production-like batching and streaming.

Technical notes & requirements (customer-specified):
- Workloads: synchronous in-editor streaming (single-turn completions), asynchronous batch indexing (embeddings generation) with high throughput, reranking for search result ordering.
- Targets: completion latency P50 < 15ms, tail P99 < 50ms; embeddings pipeline throughput 20k docs/hour sustained, spikes to 120k/hr during bulk refresh.
- Model strategy: prefer pinned open models (LLM-1.5 family); want automatic fallback to smaller quantized variant when Dedicated capacity busy.
- Operational: need prefix/KV caching for hot repos, batch coalescing for background jobs, and tooling to monitor token-level cost vs latency tradeoffs.
- Security: must support customer-managed KMS, SAML SSO, audit logs retained 1 year, and optional data residency in us-east-1.

POC plan and success criteria:
- Step 1: Redwood SE configures Dedicated cluster with same GPU class as production estimate and runs streaming completion microbench under exact concurrency and buffer sizes. Success: P99 < 60ms and functional streaming.
- Step 2: Run embedding refresh benchmark against 500k-file sample with automatic batching and KV cache disabled/enabled. Success: sustained throughput meets 20k/hr baseline and complete bulk refresh within 5 hours.
- Step 3: Security checklist validated (SOC2 evidence + KMS proof-of-concept).

Quotes / customer feedback snippets:
- "We can't have our copilot jittering — tail latency kills UX." — Head of Platform.
- "If you can show cost savings by smarter batching without hurting latency, we'll escalate." — CTO.

Open questions for Redwood:
- Behavior of auto-fallback to quantized model for streaming completions (impact on latency vs quality).
- How Dedicated handles large KV caches across GPUs and eviction behavior during burst indexing.

Next steps: schedule Dedicated perf window (block 3 hours) w/ customer infra team (target week of 2026-03-22), share detailed POC checklist and cost estimate (drive:/decks/codelattice-redwood-poc-pricing-v1).
